text:
Tanner Jeannot wears an A in Boston, and his value to the Bruins sits mostly outside the scoresheet. He's thrown 57 hits in 21 games, the kind of number that gets him profiled (NHL.com's Sunday read on the anatomy of a fight featured him and Mark Kastelic). He went undrafted and played 371 NHL games before this season, which is its own kind of story.

The scoring is thin: 1 goal and 5 points, on chances that would have expected about two goals. His rate of chances is down from last season, and he has no goals in his last ten games. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains the shape of it: he carries the puck in only a third of the time, so his line plays dump and chase.

The useful sign is the possession: at five on five the Bruins have 53.9% of the expected goals with him on. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season. Through a three-game losing streak, his job is the same as ever: make the other team's night longer.
